card.name: Subject word before a main verb
card.fires_on: A subject word or adverb sitting right before the main verb of a clause, such as a noun, pronoun or 'who' after which a verb like extend, goes, has or affects is expected. It appears in general prose and in label text.

modes.label: Noun or pronoun subject
modes.description: A subject noun or pronoun right before its verb, often inside a relative clause.
modes.example: normal ups and downs that<< everyone>> goes through from time to time.

modes.label: Adverb before verb
modes.description: An adverb placed just ahead of the verb it modifies.
modes.example: Parvovirus B19 most<< seriously>> affects pregnant women (fetal infection);

modes.label: Warning headings
modes.description: A word inside capitalized warning phrases, where a following word completes the phrase.
modes.example: BOXED WARNING WARNING: SERIOUS AND<< LIFE>>-THREATENING RISKS

card.writes: It promotes the word 'end' and its variants and suppresses 'cont' forms, with no clear link to the verb context.
card.plain: It fires on the word just before a verb is due, such as a subject or an adverb in the middle of a sentence.
